slice: Preserve Spark NULL and signed-zero behavior in ANSI Float64 division

scope.runtime: One planner file adds a native UDF adapter that checks zero with Arrow BooleanArray validity masks, then calls the existing Arrow division through DataFusion datum::apply. A proven nonzero scalar divisor simplifies to native BinaryExpr division.
scope.types: ANSI integer, float and NULL operands resolved to Float64, including existing Decimal/float coercions. Decimal/Decimal, non-ANSI, DIV and remainder keep their paths.

corpus.origin: Local numeric/NULL/zero matrix plus the prior Decimal NULL-order and analyzer cases with Decimal operands replaced by DOUBLE; duplicate SQL removed. Not an upstream CI list.

provenance.implementation_origin: Local planner adapter using installed Arrow 58.4.0 and DataFusion 54.1.0. No new Sail code was imported and no upstream PR is claimed to supply this fix.

limitations: Four original, twenty ROUND and sixty-nine new-corpus value/type or error-stage differences remain. The new corpus also exposes four existing same-stage errors with the wrong cause; the prior ROUND corpus retains its one recorded error-cause difference.

The numeric comparator checks exact ordered numeric values, types and coarse error stage, not complete schema metadata or structured error conditions. Focused checks add fifty-six new error causes and two signed-zero outputs, and preserve ninety-one earlier checks. Delta comparison separately checks names, nullability and metadata.
Non-ANSI signed zero, non-ANSI string-to-double casts and NULL/subquery evaluation order remain outside this slice.

Float execution is measured here; float planning costs are not separately timed. The four existing controls have separate planning and execution measurements. Native UDF does not mean Python row execution.

CPU frequency is not fixed and the host is not isolated. Small timing differences do not establish zero overhead; default-allocator ROUND modes must not be read as a stable kernel regression or speedup. Diagnostic allocator settings do not change production settings.
